extra.message: Mapping byte length is computed as (size_t)Long_val(words) * 8 without an overflow check. A large words count wraps size_t, under-allocates the mmap, and later region stores walk off the mapping (SIGBUS / corruption). Reject words that would overflow or use a checked multiply before mmap/ftruncate.

shm_open create path uses O_CREAT without O_EXCL. A second creator (or a retry after a crash) opens the existing object and may ftruncate it under live peers — two logical sessions share one name. Require O_CREAT|O_EXCL for exclusive create, or open existing read-only and validate generation/size before joining.

caml_failwith with a fixed string discards errno (and QNX's error detail). Callers see "MsgSendv" / "shm_open" with no strerror, which makes EAGAIN vs EINTR vs EBADF indistinguishable — the pulse EAGAIN crash is the sharp edge of this pattern. Prefer caml_uerror / caml_unix_error, or include strerror(errno) in the message.

ftruncate on a shm_open fd with O_CREAT but without O_EXCL: if the shared object already exists (e.g. a previous run or another participant sized it differently), this silently resizes shared state other processes may be using — stale/partial mappings, SIGBUS, or silent data loss. Use O_EXCL for create, or fstat and verify the existing size before truncating.

MAP_FIXED silently replaces any existing mapping overlapping the requested range — a wrong hint address can destroy the process's own address space with no error. Prefer MAP_FIXED_NOREPLACE (check EEXIST) or verify the range is free before mapping.

mmap without a matching munmap in the same function. On the success path the Bigarray may own the mapping for the process lifetime, but any failure after a successful mmap (or a missing custom finalizer) leaks the virtual mapping. Pair error paths with munmap, and ensure GC finalization calls munmap when the region is released.

extra.message: shm_open → mmap without an fstat size check between them. If the creator sized the object differently (code skew, partial create, or a new generation under the same name), mmap succeeds and the first touch past st_size delivers SIGBUS. fstat and require st_size >= expected bytes before mapping; on mismatch unmap/retry or fail cleanly.

A shared 64-bit counter is truncated to a 63-bit OCaml int. Region.unlink immediately followed by Region.create. Unconditional unlink of a well-known name creates two disconnected generations: old consumers retain the old mapping while the new producer binds a new object under the same path. Prefer unique session names (name + generation), O_CREAT|O_EXCL, layout version checks, publish READY last, and munmap before retry; never unlink-then-recreate while peers may still be mapped.

extra.message: Plain (non-atomic) store on the Merkle update path. Initialization stores are expected and excluded; update publishes leaf→root with no release store and no acquire on the reader side, so a cross-process reader can observe the new root with stale children (or a torn path). Use store_rel on the root and load_acq on reads, or document a quiescence requirement.

The copy log is an OCaml heap list consed per copied node, and the version window is a heap list too. Every Pmap.set therefore allocates on the OCaml heap in steady state — the strongest form of the "never allocate" claim does not hold for Pmap. Either scope the claim to Ring/Arena/Vclock/Merkle, or move the log into the region.

extra.message: Non-atomic check-then-store on a shared region word. Another process can modify the word between the read and the store (lost update or value inflation). Vclock.merge races this way against the owning peer's atomic fetch_add tick. Use a CAS loop or an atomic max primitive; a bare load + conditional store_rel is not atomic RMW.
